catalog_description: Initiating documents for a creative job, setting the client objective, audience, key message, deliverables, deadlines, and budget.
Assets under production within an agency job, such as images, videos, layouts, or copy, with version history and proofing and approval state.
Named variations of a creative made for testing, combining specific headline, body, image, and call-to-action choices with their own performance trail.
Definitions of digital badges and micro-credentials, covering criteria, image, issuer, and expiration policy.
Third-party verification handshakes confirming that an issued badge or credential is genuine.
Critical control points in a food-safety plan, each with its hazard, critical limit, monitoring frequency, and responsible party.
Food-traceability events along the supply chain, such as growing, receiving, transformation, and shipping, with their key data references.
People at customer or prospect organizations, carrying title, contact details, decision-maker flag, preferred channel, and opt-in state.
Prospects captured before qualification, tracking source, score, status, assigned rep, and the contact and account they would convert into.
Active sales deals, tracking stage, amount, close date, probability, products, competitor, and decision criteria.
Per-field seasonal planting plans covering crop, variety, target yield, and application schedule, including multi-year rotation history.
Dependencies between work owned by different teams that must be coordinated and resolved to keep the program on track.
Per-member, per-season farm-share subscriptions, covering share type, customization preferences, payment plan, and pickup location.
Weekly packed farm shares for a specific member, listing contents, swaps applied, packing reference, and delivery or pickup status.
Customer satisfaction, NPS, and effort survey responses tied to a case, interaction, or relationship-level survey.
Grouped learning paths and courses targeting a role, function, or compliance scope.
Derived attributes attached to a resolved customer profile, such as lifetime value, RFM score, propensity to buy, churn likelihood, and lifecycle stage.
Customer-facing support tickets, carrying severity, channel, queue, SLA clock, and references to the customer, contact, and satisfaction survey.
Records of what support a customer can use, covering service tier, monthly hours, supported channels, named contacts, and SLA response targets.
Unified stream of every customer interaction across web, mobile, email, in-product, sales, and support channels.
Qualitative or quantitative feedback from customers on product experience, gaps, or opportunities.
Single resolved customer identities consolidated across all source systems using match, merge, and survivorship rules.
Seller-issued invoices billed to customers, with line items, tax, payment terms, due date, and status from draft to paid or written off.
Observed multi-channel journeys showing how a customer moved through touchpoints over time.
Physical service locations belonging to a customer, where one customer can have many sites across properties or chains.
Customers' recurring revenue contracts, covering plan, term, MRR or ARR, billing cadence, seat count, and lifecycle from trial to churned.
Canonical records of customers, whether business accounts or end consumers, carrying identity, segmentation, lifecycle stage, and account hierarchy.
Individual cow records, covering ear tag, breed, birth date, sire and dam, parity, lactation status, and pen location.
Video-telematics incident records of AI-detected driving events such as collisions, near-misses, and distracted driving, with clips, driver, and severity.
Governance rules controlling who can access a data asset, covering audience, permission level, conditions, approval chain, and audit trail.
Cataloged data-bearing assets such as tables, datasets, APIs, databases, and files, with metadata, owner, storage location, and source system.
Attestations that a data asset meets quality and compliance thresholds for production use, with certifier, date, and valid-until.
Sensitivity tags applied to data assets, such as PII, PCI, PHI, confidential, or internal.
Right-to-erasure requests under GDPR Article 17, covering scope, anonymization policy, regulator deadline, and fulfillment status.
Logical subject-area groupings such as Customer, Order, or Inventory that organize multiple data assets with ownership and documentation.
Raw events of sensitive data being moved or accessed outside authorized boundaries, before any data-loss policy is triggered.
Flow edges linking a source data asset to a target, with column-level mapping, transformation logic, frequency, and SLA.
Data pipeline definitions and their run history, covering ingestion and transformation jobs, scheduling, dependencies, and run-level observability.
Published, governed data products with an explicit contract: schema, SLA, owner, access policy, intended consumers, and quality expectations.
Data processing addenda attached to contracts that govern how personal data is handled, each with its own approval and renewal cycle.
Per-asset risk scores combining sensitivity, access breadth, and exposure, used to prioritize the remediation queue.
Assignments of a steward to a data asset or glossary term, with responsibility type and escalation chain.
Privacy rights requests from candidates exercising access, rectification, erasure, restriction, portability, or objection, with intake, due date, and fulfillment.
Aggregated consumption signals per data asset, such as accessing team, query count, last access, and bytes scanned.
Cloud analytics databases or clusters specialized for analytics, with an access model distinct from transactional databases.
Cabinets within data center racks, covering layout, power distribution, cable management, access control, and temperature zones.
Physical cable connections between ports, covering length, type, installation date, test state, and failure history.
Forward-looking projections of data center power, cooling, space, and bandwidth capacity, with utilization forecast, headroom, and planned augmentations.
Requests to install, decommission, or relocate data center equipment, carrying the action, target rack, scheduling, and approval before physical work.
Data center cooling units such as CRAC, CRAH, or in-row coolers, with capacity, zone served, temperature setpoints, and power draw.
Time-series temperature, humidity, airflow, and pressure readings from cabinet, aisle, and zone sensors for hot-spot detection.
Network or power ports on a device, covering interface name, speed and type, neighbor endpoint, assignment, and usage status.
Electrical circuits from the site feed to a power outlet, covering capacity, voltage, phase, breaker state, and redundancy.
Rack or cabinet power distribution units, covering input phases, output outlets, per-outlet metering, management mode, and firmware version.
Physical rack frames in a data center, covering height in rack units, location, power budget, cooling zone, and asset tag.
Uninterruptible power supply units, covering input and output capacity, battery health, last test date, load level, and bypass state.
Dynamic creative optimization rule sets governing how variants are generated from assets and feeds and how delivery is weighted toward top performers.
Per-opportunity machine-derived risk grades with the contributing factors, recomputed as new activity and signals arrive.
Named risk patterns raised against an opportunity, such as no decision-maker or no scheduled next step, tracked from raised to cleared.
Recorded runtime evaluations of a decision table against a set of inputs, capturing matched rules, resulting outputs, and the invoking process.
Versioned decision tables with input and output clauses, rules, and a hit policy, invoked by running processes to evaluate business rules.
Configurable definitions of pay deductions such as retirement, medical premiums, garnishments, and union dues, with priority, ceiling, and ledger mapping.
Detected constraints or slow stages in a value stream surfaced from measured flow and prioritized for remediation.
Optimized multi-stop delivery routes per delivery day, covering vehicle, driver, stops, and time windows.
Modeled end-to-end paths that delivery work flows through, from idea to production, used as the unit of flow measurement.
Business cases submitted for new initiatives or features, covering requester, justification, estimated cost, timeline, and approval workflow.
Sequencing and blocking relationships between initiatives and roadmap items, covering critical path, lag time, and external dependencies.
Self-service desk reservations for hybrid and hot-desking workplaces, covering the desk, date and time, and work mode.
Records of which mobile app packages are pushed to which enrolled devices, with install status, timestamp, and removal flag.
Accuracy verification records for clinical equipment such as scales and infusion pumps, tracking calibration date, technician, and tolerance acceptance.
Baseline policies defining required device state, such as OS version floor, encryption, app blocklist, root detection, and password rules.
Periodic compliance scan results per enrolled device, listing policies evaluated, pass or fail per policy, findings, and remediation actions.
Device settings templates covering WiFi, VPN, certificates, security baselines, and disk encryption, version-controlled and assigned to device cohorts.
Outcome logs for each policy, profile, or app deployment, covering trigger, timestamp, success flag, error code, and device state change.
Adverse-event reports for medical devices, such as patient injury or unexpected behavior, with root cause and links to recalls when patterns emerge.
Preventive and corrective maintenance records per medical device, covering schedule completion, technician notes, and parts replaced.
Regulatory recall notices and facility responses for medical devices, covering recall scope, risk class, affected serials, and patient-safety impact.
Images, videos, audio, documents, and design files with metadata, rights, taxonomy, and delivery URLs.
Named digital experiences or journeys, such as a post-purchase flow, mapped to segments and A/B variants.
Detected degradations affecting app usage, such as slow boot, crashes, login failures, network drops, or VPN issues, with severity and affected users.
Logical entity, dimension, and hierarchy models decoupled from physical tables, defining conformed dimensions, hierarchies, and slowly-changing behavior.
State-mandated and brokerage-policy disclosure forms attached to transactions, such as agency, property condition, lead paint, and HOA documents.
Workflow records gating discount authority, capturing the approver and the accept or reject decision.
Candidate devices emitted by a scan, awaiting normalization and reconciliation into a configuration item before joining the CMDB.
Process models mined from an event log via process discovery, carrying fitted parameters and quality metrics such as fitness and precision.
Records of a discovery job run, covering scope, credentials used, start and end times, candidates emitted, and errors encountered.
Connector, probe, and credential definitions for discovery integrations such as hypervisors, cloud accounts, clusters, and directory services.
Assignments of a work order to a specific technician at a specific time, capturing dispatch decisions, route output, and dispatcher overrides.
Post-call wrap-up categories that classify the business reason for a contact, used for routing logic and analytics.
End-to-end request traces across microservices, with parent-child spans, service identification, and latency attribution for diagnosing issues.
Investor-facing notice documents for a fund distribution, in standard reporting format, with publication timestamps.
Approved, time-limited exceptions to a data-loss policy, tracking requestor, approver, business justification, and expiration.
Data-loss policy violation events, capturing user, timestamp, classification, destination, action taken, and remediation status.
Data-loss prevention rule sets defining conditions and actions such as block, quarantine, redact, mask, watermark, or alert.
Blocked or flagged artifacts such as emails, files, or messages held pending admin review or a user override request.
Audit trail of user interactions with the data-loss system, covering blocks, quarantine reviews, exception requests, and policy violations.
Invoices issued to boaters for dockage, storage, utilities, fuel, or service, with payment status.
Outputs of document-type classification, capturing the classified type, confidence, model version, and timestamp.
